items.title: Iran war derailed talks to claw back billions in tax credits paid to miners
items.description: Billions in tax credits are paid to coal miners every year. Ministers discussed clawing back some of that money in the May federal budget, but the Iran war has pushed out those talks.

items.title: The BHP files reveal a big problem facing the mining giant
items.description: For a company that prides itself on digging out the metals for the world's clean energy future, saying nothing about its own clean energy future is not an option.

items.title: Woman in nine-year battle with insurer as failed roof repairs cause mould
items.description: Lily lodged an insurance claim with her provider GIO Suncorp after a truck ran through her street's power lines. Nearly a decade later, she has been forced out of her home.

items.title: Women and children linked to ISIS spend first night back in Australia
items.description: A group of so-called ISIS brides who left the notorious al-Roj camp in Syria last week have spent their first night home in Australia.

items.title: Despite growing up online, students' digital literacy is declining
items.description: Australian students have recorded their worst-ever results in national tests that measure digital literacy, with just 37 per cent of year 10 students and 50 per cent of year 6 students assessed as proficient.

items.title: Report claims AI boom could keep Australia using coal and gas for longer
items.description: A new report concludes the AI-fuelled surge of power-hungry data centres across Australia is jeopardising the country's energy transition.

items.title: Scott's sacking gives Essendon another chance to step out of Hird shadow
items.description: Essendon finds itself at a clear demarcation point after sacking Brad Scott as the shadow of James Hird once again looms large over the troubled club.

items.title: Complaint lodged with Canada's privacy commissioner over Australian court breach
items.description: Litigants in at least 146 court matters were potentially involved in a data breach that is now the subject of a formal complaint with the privacy commissioner in Canada, Senate estimates has been told.

items.title: Europe bakes in unprecedented heatwave as UK records tumble
items.description: The British capital's previous hottest May day was set only one day prior, when the mercury topped 33.5C.

items.title: 'Very scary and sad': Travellers in limbo after company enters liquidation
items.description: An Australian travel company selling heavily discounted international holidays has collapsed, leaving customers scrambling and their plans in disarray.

items.title: Navy chief says Chinese flotilla in Tasman Sea had 'impact'
items.description: Australia's Chief of Navy says China stirred "anger" in New Zealand when it sent a powerful naval flotilla into the Tasman Sea last year, encouraging political support on both sides of the ditch for increased defence spending.

items.title: State of Origin is tonight. Here is what you need to know for Game I
items.description: The fiercest rival in Australian rugby league resumes tonight, as New South Wales and Queensland meet in the opening match of the 2026 men's State of Origin series.

items.title: Wallabies facing same selection headache as State of Origin's NSW Blues
items.description: Just as NSW Blues coach Laurie Daley had a difficult selection decision to make, Joe Schmidt may be thinking long and hard about one position in the Wallabies' back line for July's Nations Championship Tests.

items.title: CBA boss says reconsider applying CGT change to non-passive assets
items.description: The Commonwealth Bank boss speaks out about the government's tax changes.

items.title: What to do when you get unexpected ancestry DNA test results
items.description: Direct-to-consumer genetic testing kits are often given as gifts or purchased "as a bit of fun", which means people often aren't prepared to discover unexpected parents, siblings and other relatives.

items.title: Blak Douglas is an Archibald winner. He says the art prize needs to change
items.description: The acclaimed Dunghutti artist is using his latest exhibition to challenge perceptions of Aboriginal art and the systemic issues creatives face in Australia.

items.title: Quiz: Who has scored more tries in State of Origin games in Sydney?
items.description: If you think you know your stuff when it comes to State of Origin, here's your chance to prove it.

items.title: US military strikes Iranian boats and missile launch sites
items.description: US Centcom says the strikes were designed "to protect our troops from threats posed by Iranian forces".

items.title: Bondi gunman remained on counter-terror radar in 2022
items.description: Naveed Akram and his father travelled to Uzbekistan around 2022 and a former terror hotspot in the Philippines shortly before committing the Bondi massacre.

items.title: Four dead, including two children, after train hits Belgian school bus
items.description: The train collided with a minibus, which was carrying nine people at the time, at a level crossing.

items.title: Archibald Prize sitter calls out APY art collective mistreatment
items.description: Award-winning artist Iluwanti Ken says the withdrawal of funding and support over the "white hands on black art" scandal has left her feeling like a stranger in her own industry.

items.title: Iron ore processing project dumped by BHP for not being profitable enough
items.description: Internal BHP documents reveal how the mining giant planned to set up an iron ore processing facility in the Pilbara to cut carbon emissions before backing away from it entirely.

items.title: One woman will make Japanese history by going on maternity leave
items.description: A Japanese mayor will take maternity leave this year, becoming the first in the country's history to do so while in office.

items.title: When moving forward means being the cycle-breaker in a family
items.description: Motherhood has a way of making family patterns impossible to ignore. Suddenly you start asking questions you never asked before.

items.title: Reception hours slashed at police stations in Melbourne's outer-north
items.description: Victoria Police says its decision to cut the hours police stations are open to the public in Melbourne's outer north will result in more police on the frontline.
